const bodies={
47:`**Goal**  
A user can save an active workout session on their device, resume it after a relaunch, and retrieve finished or stopped sessions as workout history.

**Context**  
Part of #33. Replaces the workout-session portion of #24 and session storage work from #25. The on-device model follows #136 and ADR 0006. #48 owns the workout screens and navigation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Add versioned SQLite storage and typed service operations for starting, reopening, and finalizing workout sessions, and for listing and reading workout history.
- [ ] Create a session from a saved workout template with independent copies of exercise details, ordered session exercises, and target performance. Editing or deleting the template leaves the session intact.
- [ ] Allow one active session. Persist validated recorded performance asynchronously when the user checks a session set. Restore only successfully saved checked sets after a relaunch.
- [ ] Preserve start and finish or stop timestamps and distinguish completed from stopped sessions. Keep active sessions available for resumption and add completed or stopped sessions to workout history.
- [ ] Surface recoverable errors so the workout flow can retain entered values and offer retry. Verify a retry does not duplicate a session or recorded set.
- [ ] Verify active and completed session persistence, checked-set recovery, and independent history across SQLite reopen. Use the existing route and native seams agreed in #136.

**Where to start**  
The SQLite workout service and migrations from #141, ADR 0003 on independent workout history, and the workout session glossary entries.

**Dependencies**  
#141 is the template-parity gate. This ticket unblocks #48.`,
48:`**Goal**  
A user can start a workout from a saved template, log sets, resume an interrupted session, and review a finished or stopped session in history.

**Context**  
Part of #33. Replaces the workout-screen portion of #23. Use the SQLite session service from #47 and the single-device behavior agreed in #136. Preserve the session detail behavior delivered in #64.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Start from a saved workout template and show its exercises, planned sets, and workout duration.
- [ ] Let the user enter actual reps and weight and check an indicator to log the set. Keep rapid logging responsive. If the write fails, retain entered values and show Retry.
- [ ] Return directly to the active workout when the user comes back from the background. After a force-close or an app update that relaunches the app, show a prominent **Resume workout** action on Templates.
- [ ] Restore successfully saved checked sets on resume. Offer to resume or stop the existing active session before starting another.
- [ ] Let the user finish or stop at any time. Compute duration from the start timestamp to the finish or stop timestamp, including time away.
- [ ] Show completed and stopped sessions in workout history with exercise and set details. Keep history independent of later template edits or deletion.
- [ ] Verify start, rapid set logging, failure and retry, background return, cold-launch recovery, elapsed duration, finish or stop, and history. Use a supported physical device for the offline and app lifecycle checks agreed in #136.

**Where to start**  
The existing Templates and workout history screens and the session service from #47.

**Dependencies**  
#38, #47, #46. The #141 cutover gate applies through #47.`,
49:`**Goal**  
A user's personal exercise maximums and percentage-based template targets survive app restarts and can be used for target-weight calculation.

**Context**  
Part of #37. Replaces the exercise maximum portion of #24 and related storage work from #25. Extend the on-device SQLite template service from #141 under #136. #37 tracks the calculation and user-facing percentage-planning behavior.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Add versioned SQLite migrations and TypeScript contracts for personal exercise maximums keyed by catalog exercise identity and for fixed-weight and percentage-based template targets.
- [ ] Implement saving, updating, and reading personal exercise maximums through the injected asynchronous service.
- [ ] Save a template's percentage target atomically with the template aggregate. On reopen, retain the percentage for calculation from the personal exercise maximum.
- [ ] Validate values at the service boundary and return a defined missing-maximum result to the calculation and UI layer.
- [ ] Verify maximums and percentage targets round-trip through real SQLite after reopening the database, with fixed-weight templates preserved through the schema upgrade.

**Where to start**  
The SQLite template service and migrations verified in #141 and the glossary entries for personal exercise maximum and percentage-based target.

**Dependencies**  
#141 is the template-parity gate.`
};

}

# Local onboarding and SQLite verification

[#141](https://github.com/open-source-fitness/open-fit/issues/141) switches the
production app to local display-name onboarding and uses SQLite for workout
templates. The app ships the RepDB catalog and flat illustrations. Workout
history still shows labeled samples.

## Verified in the worktree

- On Node 24.12.0, `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` (109 tests in 22
  suites), and `npx expo-doctor` (20 checks) passed.
- The Expo Router tests start the default app with a fresh database and use
  Node's SQLite engine with the Expo SQLite bridge substituted. With JavaScript
  fetch disabled, the tests dismiss the device storage and backup pop-up, require
  a nonblank display name, greet the user on Templates, inspect both poses of a
  bundled exercise, and save a template. They close the database, remount the
  app, reopen the template, edit it, and delete it.
- A pre-cutover SQLite schema version 2 fixture retains its saved template and
  set targets after migration. A name edited in Settings and the Dark
  appearance both survive an app remount. The remaining SQLite and router
  tests cover draft navigation, cancellation, reordering, snapshots, rollback,
  save retries, and sample history.
- Both iOS and Android Expo exports passed with the Supabase environment
  variables unset, dotenv loading disabled, and Expo offline mode enabled.
  Each bundle contains the local SQLite composition and RepDB instructions.
  Both export manifests reference all 1,203 RepDB illustrations, totaling
  19,804,900 bytes before application packaging. The Hermes bundles measure
  5,327,488 bytes for iOS and 5,317,600 for Android. Source maps contain no
  Supabase runtime or legacy account routes.
- Android release assembly passed from a clean copy of cutover revision
  `644b22d` using Expo prebuild and Gradle. The resulting universal APK was
  127,559,668 bytes. All 1,231 packaged RepDB illustrations matched their source
  WebP files by SHA-256. The APK was inspected locally without installing it.

At the time of this verification, the retired account implementation was
still present in the worktree.
`auth-navigation.test.tsx`, `auth-sessions.test.tsx`, and
`production-template-access.test.tsx` exercise the retired router and are
excluded from the active Jest and TypeScript checks for this run.

## Physical-device evidence pending

No iOS or Android device was available. Neither platform ran an installed build
during this verification. The native Expo SQLite bridge, first launch and
catalog rendering in airplane mode, force-close recovery, in-place app update,
and installed package size remain unverified. The database migration and
restart checks above ran through Jest. Follow the
[device-review steps](setup.md#device-review) to complete the offline

const body=`## Description

OpenFit now opens with local display-name onboarding, uses SQLite for workout templates, and ships the attributed RepDB catalog and illustrations for offline use. Existing template screens keep their create, read, edit, delete, and retry behavior. Workout history remains labeled sample data until the M2 session work.

\`\`\`text
Name onboarding → Templates → injected service → SQLite
                             ↘ bundled RepDB catalog and illustrations
\`\`\`

## Related Issue Link

Closes #136. Closes #138. Closes #139. Closes #140. Closes #141. Closes #142. Closes #143.

- #145 reviews the offline exercise catalog (#138).
- #146 reviews SQLite template creation and reads (#139).
- #147 reviews SQLite template editing and deletion (#140).
- #148 reviews the production SQLite and name onboarding cutover (#141).
- #149 reviews retirement of the Supabase contributor workflow (#143).
- #150, #151, and #152 review Supabase app cleanup (#142) in three slices under 1,000 lines each.

The M2 briefs in #47, #48, and #49 now describe the SQLite and resume behavior. #141 remains the physical-device template-parity gate.

## PR Checklist

- [x] Changes are available as individual review slices
- [x] Integrated TypeScript and offline iOS and Android exports pass
- [x] All 99 Jest tests and 20 Expo Doctor checks pass
- [x] Setup and architecture documentation reflect the cutover
- [ ] Physical-device offline template-parity audit
- [ ] Review from one non-author contributor

## Additional Details

### Evidence

- The default router flow runs with JavaScript fetch disabled and uses real SQLite files via Node. It covers name entry, bundled illustrations, template CRUD, save retries, reopening, and schema upgrades. The native Expo SQLite bridge still requires the installed-app audit.
- The final integration rejects foreign and invented saved placement IDs and retains an unchanged committed retry after a newer edit removes a placement.
- Both final Expo exports passed with Supabase environment variables unset. Android release assembly passed for the cutover revision, and all 1,231 packaged RepDB illustrations matched the source files by SHA-256.
- No physical iOS or Android device was connected. The [device review](https://github.com/open-source-fitness/open-fit/blob/feat/136-local-storage/docs/setup.md#device-review) documents the remaining airplane-mode, force-close, and installed-update scenarios.

### Merge Danger

**Door** Two-way for the code. The cutover starts with an empty SQLite database. The previous hosted records are disposable test data and stay outside this PR.

**Blast radius** App startup, template persistence, and exercise catalog delivery.
`;

<t3_code_orchestration_01>## T3 Code orchestration

Ordinary coding tasks need no T3 tools.

- Subagents: use your native tool when the child uses your provider, a model it offers and no settings beyond yours (Claude `Agent`, `run_in_background:false`; Codex `spawn_agent`, then wait). Use `delegate_task` for another provider's model, user-asked settings, a separate checkout (`isolation:"worktree"`), or `delegate_task` by name. A native type on another provider's model counts too. Background agent: `delegate_task`, never a background `Agent`. Workflow only when asked.
- Call `orchestrator_capabilities` once per thread, before the first `delegate_task`. Again only after an error or a user-named provider change. Settings go in `target.options`. Provider or model unavailable: say so. Never switch unasked or fall back to native tools, Workflow or CLIs. Never make a child's checkout in the shell or in `task`.
- Every new delegate review or re-check is a new `delegate_task` (brief, findings, objections), never a `t3_thread_send`. Fix small review findings yourself; start no delegate for them. When told to proceed without a delegate, or to run fewer, `task_cancel` the extras. Start no replacement.
- Follow a running delegate's `next`. Don't poll it (`task_status`, `sleep`, watchers, Monitor, ScheduleWakeup). Stop a delegate run you replace or no longer need with `task_cancel`, never `t3_thread_interrupt` on a `childThreadId`.
- As a subagent or child, do the work yourself. Start no subagents unless your task says to.</t3_code_orchestration_01>

<t3_code_orchestration_02>- `t3_thread_launch` and `create_threads` make new top-level threads, only when the user asks for a new thread. "Subagent", "delegate", and "parallel" never mean one. Worktree thread: set `workspaceStrategy`. Honor a requested base. Otherwise independent work uses the default branch as `remote/branch` with `startFromOrigin:true`; with no remote, use the local default. Required unpublished commits and dependent work use their local base. Shell worktrees don't bind it, and no checkout setup in its prompt. No `workspaceStrategy`: project root, not your worktree.
- Given a thread id, `t3_thread_read` it before you answer about it. Asked to settle a thread, this one too: `t3_thread_organize`.
- Another machine: `t3_environment_links` lists linked ones. Pass its `environmentId` and that machine's `threadId` to T3 tools.
- Unlinked ("delegate this to my vps"): `t3_environment_link` with a `hint` from the user's words, never a pairing code in chat. No link tools: say to enable Settings → Labs → Linked environments.
- In your reply, mention a thread by its `link`, verbatim, never a plain title or bare id.
- A login, token, PIN, pairing code or sudo password only the user can give: call `request_secret`, not a chat ask or a handoff. Not for access you have. Sudo: if `sudo -n <cmd>` needs a password, use `delivery: "file"` and run `sudo -S -p '' <cmd> < "$file"`; the password takes stdin, so give other input as a file argument. Asked only to schedule: `schedule_task` without running its prompt.
- T3 tools may load late. Try the name once before you call it absent.</t3_code_orchestration_02>

<t3_code_orchestration_03>### Visuals and preview

- Answer data with a trend or comparison with a chart and show any visual the user asks for here: pass an HTML file path or inline HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. A screenshot on disk or a text description doesn't show it. Never start a server for it. Page tools write only on user request. Never use them to show results. Asked for an image to post, send or use elsewhere: a `.png` file and its path, never `html_render`.
- Never use `preview_*` unasked to verify or show your own edit. Use them when the current request asks for browser work, including recording edits, or names a page or tab. Don't repeat preview calls from an earlier turn. Public pages: web fetch or search unless browser work was asked; then preview tools only, no web fetch. Close a tab you opened before you reply, unless the user asked for it or uses it.</t3_code_orchestration_03>

<t3_code_runtime><runtime_info>In case you're asked: you are running in T3 Code through the Codex harness, as gpt-6.2-sol with medium reasoning effort. No need to mention this otherwise. You can embed images, video, and audio using Markdown image syntax with absolute file paths. Link every other file you cite or produce by its absolute path, as in [http.ts:42](/abs/path/http.ts:42), so the user can open it in T3 Code's files viewer.</runtime_info>

<pull_request_linking>
Link each PR you create, take over, or push to: link_pull_request, or link_pull_requests for several, full URL, every stack layer, as your next call. Host tools don't link for you. If linking fails, say so. Skip PRs you only read or review and PRs named only as background. Call watch_pull_request when asked to monitor or babysit, or when work you were asked to do, such as a merge, still waits on checks or reviews, even after an earlier unwatch. Finish any needed branch update and push first, then watch and end your turn. Otherwise act now or hand back. Delegated children never watch, even if the brief says babysit. After PR work, a child's last line is: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>. Links and watches persist across pushes. For PR waits, no sleep, loops, gh --watch, Monitor or ScheduleWakeup. Before handback, call unwatch_pull_request on any PR you watch.
</pull_request_linking></t3_code_runtime>

<t3_code_tools>

## T3 Code browser

When browser work was asked, `preview_*` is the browser you share with the user: `preview_status` first, then `preview_open` if no tab can be automated. Prefer snapshot locators over coordinates. Switch browsers only if the tools are absent or `preview_open` says unsupported, the user asks, or two preview calls fail on one step. Then quote the error and switch.
